gaps.text: No real fabric or plastic sample was burned at the O2 level of Lunar base (30 % O2, 70.3 kPa).
gaps.evidence: 46 tests near this atmosphere: 0 solid, 41 droplet, 5 gas (only droplets and gas flames); 0 solid-fuel rows within ±6 percentage points of O2 even ignoring pressure. Solids (fabrics, plastics) are the main fire load in a habitat.
gaps.closest_proxy: ACME BRE (PSI-20), a gas burner emulating a PMMA-like solid, burned steadily in microgravity at 26.5 % O2 / 70.3 kPa (test 19070K1) and 34 % O2 / 56.5 kPa (test 19070D1) - BRE Final Report 2022, pp. 25-26: 'a common plastic could steadily burn under these NASA proposed atmospheric conditions'.

gaps.text: Solid materials were tested only up to 22.2 % O2, below every planned exploration atmosphere (30–34 % O2).
gaps.evidence: 143 O2 values in 3 solid-fuel investigations with an O2 column; range 13.6–22.2 %. The BASS (PSI-26) table records no O2 at all. Closest proxy: ACME BRE (PSI-20), a gas burner emulating a PMMA-like solid, burned steadily in microgravity at 34 % O2 / 56.5 kPa (test 19070D1) - BRE Final Report 2022, pp. 25-26: 'a common plastic could steadily burn under these NASA proposed atmospheric conditions'.

gaps.text: No solid-material test has a recorded pressure in the PSI tables.
gaps.evidence: 0 of 380 solid-fuel rows have a pressure value (BASS, BASS-II, SAFFIRE and SAME tables have no pressure column).

gaps.text: No partial-gravity (Moon 1/6 g, Mars 3/8 g) combustion data in PSI — and 0 g / 1 g results may not bound it.
gaps.evidence: All 19 flight investigations ran in microgravity; ACME E-FIELD (PSI-22) uses electric fields only as a proxy. The challenge text says 0 g and 1 g results 'could bound' partial gravity, but that is not guaranteed: in microgravity, concurrent flame spread is most vigorous at an intermediate, low flow speed (the 'Goldilocks' flammability zone of Olson and Ferkul, PSI-62), and the weak buoyant flow at lunar or Martian gravity is also low speed, so a partial-gravity case could be worse than both. NASA's newer analysis finds lunar gravity 'nearly the most flammable condition' (Ferkul, Kralik, Liao & Johnston, LPSC 2026, NTRS 20260001966, slide 17). Planned NASA experiments LUCI and FM2 are meant to measure it.

gaps.text: Nothing was tested at spacesuit conditions (100 % O2, 29.6 kPa).
gaps.evidence: Highest atmosphere O2 in any test: 40 %. (Inverse flames in PSI-10 / PSI-159 blow up to 85 % O2 out of the burner into a fuel atmosphere - that is not a cabin atmosphere.) 0 tests near spacesuit conditions.
